section_new.excerpt: ## Why this can look like a lock problem A pinned waiter holds a carrier while it waits. A signaled virtual thread that has been unmounted needs a free carrier before it can run. If every carrier is occupied by pinned waiters, the signaled thread cannot make progress even when the lock itself has been released. An observer may then see a live process, an apparently free lock and no completed requests. That is a scheduler/resource interlock, not necessarily a permanently held mutex. This diagnostic framing is Tycho synthesis. section_new.excerpt: ## Why replacing a pool looked appealing Virtual threads preserve direct-looking synchronous Java programming while allowing many *I/O-blocked* requests to yield their carrier platform threads. A migration from a bounded OS-thread executor to a per-task virtual-thread executor can therefore reduce the need for large platform-thread pools when tasks spend much of their lives waiting for sockets.
